mutations.because: V3's split is worthless if a thread that appears in two workflows is pinned on the first one that happened to match. Taking matches[0] on length >= 1 turns an unattributed collision into a false UI (or API) count, which is exactly the guess the fail-closed rule exists to refuse. Caught by the two-logs test asserting unattributed, not UI.
command: text present in two logs is unattributed, never the first match

mutations.because: The job log stores the model's response JSON-escaped (\n, \", \u2011). Matching the thread's plain suggestion against the raw log misses every quote, every newline, and the non-breaking hyphen PR-Agent actually writes, so a real API thread looks unattributed. Caught by the escape test, whose log is the escaped form of the thread text.

mutations.after: // mutated: a truncated run list is no longer refused
mutations.because: A list that returns exactly the limit is incomplete: older runs are unsearched. Treating it as complete can hide a second workflow's match and turn a true ambiguity into a false single attribution. The refusal must stay. Caught by the at-limit test, which names the workflow and exits 1.
command: a run list of exactly the limit exits 1, naming the workflow

mutations.after: // mutated: a foreign headSha is no longer ignored
mutations.because: Runs selected by branch name alone pull in an older PR that reused the head-branch name. That older log can supply a match the current PR's runs do not, and a missing current-PR log then looks like a single attribution. Caught by the foreign-headSha test: the thread that matched only the other PR's run is unattributed.
command: a run whose headSha is not among the PR's commits is ignored
